_note: Skeleton for docs/ontology-exemptions.json — the factory data file read by tests/test_ontology.py. Copy it into docs/ (the example itself is never read) and fill it ONLY with roots and lines YOUR factory actually has: a `dated_artifacts` root that is not an existing directory is a gate ERROR, because a class whose root is absent excludes nothing and must not pass silently, and an `exemptions` entry that matches 0 hits is a gate ERROR too, because a stale exemption excuses nothing. `dated_artifacts` names DIRECTORIES whose files are DATED RECORDS — a survey, a score, a review written at an instant and never rewritten. A vocabulary gate cannot judge those: the banned word inside one is the evidence that the drift happened. They are EXCLUDED from judgement and COUNTED in the gate's own output (`dated: <path> (N hit(s) not judged)`), so an exclusion is never silent. An `exemptions` entry names ONE line inside a document that is NOT a dated record, where the banned term is QUOTED rather than used, and it carries all four fields — path, substring, reason, proof — because a path and a substring without a reason and a proof is forgiveness, not a declaration: `proof` must point at something a reader can OPEN (a file and the line or section that shows the quoted term). Paths are exact and matched literally; there are NO globs, deliberately, so an exemption cannot quietly widen into a class. This file ships EMPTY on purpose: the four entries and the two roots in this repo's own copy are ITS records (evidence/scores/ and reviews/ are this factory's dated classes, and the quoted lines are in its own documents) — a fresh factory has neither those files nor that history, so copying them in would red its gate on its first run.
